column3: The Hebrew written text has הַמַּלְאֿכִים (“messengers”); NASB follows the reading “kings.” “At the return of the year” is rendered “in the spring,” and NASB supplies “to battle.”
“At the time of evening” is rendered “when evening came.”
The Hebrew “she was purifying herself” is rendered “when she had purified herself.”
“The welfare of the battle” is rendered “the state of the war.”
“A gift of the king went out” is rendered “a present from the king was sent out.”
“Booths” is rendered “temporary shelters,” and the oath “if I will do” as “I will not do.”
“To the front of the face of the battle” is rendered “in the front line,” and “severe” as “fiercest.”
“Matters of the battle” is rendered “events of the war.”
“Matters of the battle” is rendered “events of the war.”
“We were on them” is rendered “we pressed them.”
“Like this and like this” is rendered “one as well as another.”
“Gathered her” is rendered “brought her,” and “displeasing” as “evil.”
